text:
maria: quick sanity check — onboarding mixtral-v2-6b. I pushed weights to s3://redwood-models/mixtral-v2/2026-02-14/weights/ and published via the model-publish job, but in local serving tests I'm seeing an extra BOS token duplicated when using chat templates + prefix caching. @devin @sam any ideas? :eyes:

devin: hm. two things to check quickly: runtime expects a model dir with model.bin (or shards), params.json, and tokenizer.json/tokenizer.model depending on tokenizer type. If your model-card has explicit special tokens that differ from tokenizer.json that can cause duplicates. Do you have model_card.yaml or model_config.json in that dir? Also posting the exact prompt sample helps.

maria: there is a model_card.yaml at the weights root, snippet: ```
name: mixtral-v2-6b
special_tokens:
  bos_token: "<|BOS|>"
  eos_token: "<|EOS|>"
  pad_token: "<|PAD|>"
```
But tokenizer.json (from huggingface export) lists bos_token as null and eos_token as "". Weird mismatch.

sam: can you paste the chat template you're using? sometimes templates add <s> or <|system|> tokens and our prompt-prepend step also adds a BOS.

maria: using minimal chat template: ```
[system]
You are an assistant.
[/system]

[user]
{{user_message}}
[/user]
```
(we replace tags with tokens in the launcher: `<|system|>` => `bos+system_marker` etc). Repro steps: 1) send system+user as a single input with prefix caching enabled 2) server returns stream and the first chunk contains two copies of <|BOS|> (or token id for BOS twice) 3) when I disable prefix cache the duplicate goes away.

sam: ok that points to double-insertion: tokenizer or launcher is adding a leading BOS and prefix cache already stores an initial BOS token from the cached KV. Two mitigation paths: make tokenizer not auto-add BOS on encode (some HF tokenizers have `add_bos_token=True`), or change launcher/runtime flag `auto_add_bos=false`. In our serving runtime the config option is `encoding.auto_add_special_tokens` which defaults to true for chat presets. Try `encoding.auto_add_special_tokens=false` in the model config under `runtime_opts`.

devin: also watch out for mismatch between the vocabulary token used for "BOS" and the one used when building the cache. Our caching layer stores token ids, so if model_card lists "<|BOS|>" but tokenizer serialized uses "<s>" as bos, you'll see weird duplicates or wrong prepends. Run the validator: ```sh
redwood model-validate --path /mnt/models/mixtral-v2-20260214 --expect-special bos,eos,pad
```
Expected output excerpt: ```
tokenizer.special_tokens: {"bos": "<|BOS|>", "eos": "<|EOS|>"}
cache.prepend_ids: [bos_id]
```
If the validate command flags a mismatch, sync model_card to tokenizer.json and re-run publish.

infra-bot: model-publish pipeline finished: mixtral-v2-6b @ s3://redwood-models/mixtral-v2/2026-02-14/weights/ mirrored -> /mnt/models/mixtral-v2-20260214 (snapshot id: snap-20260214-3).

devin: another edge: HF tokenizers sometimes encode ``""`` as eos but leave bos null; when we canonicalize special tokens into integer ids we must prefer tokenizer.json over model_card.yaml. If you have both, runtime will prefer tokenizer.json unless `trust_model_card: true` is set. I recommend updating tokenizer.json to include explicit bos_token (quick hack: `tokenizer._tokenizer.post_processor_add_bos = True` on export or a small edit).

jeff: can we add a unit test in the onboarding CI that loads published model from /mnt/models/... and asserts: 1) tokenizer.encode(system_prefix)[0] == bos_id 2) streaming chunks do not start with bos_id if prefix cache is present? Pseudocode: ```py
def test_no_duplicate_bos(tmp_path):
    model_dir = "/mnt/models/mixtral-v2-20260214"
    tok = Tokenizer.from_file(os.path.join(model_dir, "tokenizer.json"))
    bos_id = tok.token_to_id("<|BOS|>")
    cached_prefix = tok.encode("<|BOS|><|system|>You are an assistant.")
    out = run_inference_with_prefix_cache(model_dir, cached_prefix, "Hello")
    assert out.token_ids[0] != bos_id
```
I'll open a quick PR for the test.

maria: perfect — I'll open a PR that: 1) updates tokenizer.json to include bos_token matching model_card 2) sets runtime opts `encoding.auto_add_special_tokens=false` in model config 3) adds jeff's unit test. tagging this thread in the PR. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — if you want me to run the `model-validate` check in CI I can add it as a step. Also add a small note in onboarding playbook: "if you see duplicated BOS with prefix cache, check tokenizer.bos vs model_card and runtime.auto_add_special_tokens".

maria: will do. filing with label `model-onboard` + `bug`. link: https://git.redwood.dev/r/redwood/models/pulls/842 :link:

devin: once PR lands, can we do a quick smoke test on dedicated qa cluster to verify streaming + replay? I'll ping infra for a short slot.

infra-bot: scheduled smoke test job 21893 on qa-dedicated-02 in 10m.

maria: awesome, thanks all. I'll post results here after smoke test.
